title: Network Disconnection Mapper
scopeNote: This keeps the live network model, because breaking something and watching the consequence cannot be replaced by a diagram of the answer. A fourth region and task, pathways serving more than one pairing, and the backwards exercise inferring the break from the pattern stay in the longer version.
summary: Three regions joined by three pathways, and three tasks that each need two regions and the pathway between them. Damaging a region takes out the tasks that share it; cutting a pathway takes out one task with both its regions intact.
learningObjectives: Explain how a deficit can arise from a disconnection rather than from damage to any region.
Read the pattern of which tasks fail as evidence about where the break is.
Explain why a selective deficit with normal-looking grey matter is a reason to look at white matter.
Recognise that asking which region does a job can be the wrong question.
State what a three-region cartoon does and does not license about real anatomy.
interactionTypes: six live toggles damaging regions or cutting pathways
a network diagram redrawn on every change
three task outcomes updating live with the reason each one failed
a guided setting showing the disconnection case directly
a withheld explanation released once something has been broken
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout: the network is manipulated by six labelled checkboxes rather than by clicking the diagram, so nothing depends on pointing at a small target, and each checkbox names what it does. A damaged region is drawn with a broken outline and a cross as well as a colour, and a cut pathway is drawn as two stubs with a visible gap and a cross, so no break is signalled by colour alone. The diagram carries a description listing every damaged region, every cut pathway and every failing task, so the state is fully available as text. Each task tile states works or fails in words and gives the reason. Every change is announced through a polite live region. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
dataStatus: A deliberately simplified cartoon. The regions, pathways and tasks are named for teaching and do not describe a real anatomy or a real patient.
simulationNotes: Each task needs two regions and exactly one pathway, which is what makes the two kinds of break distinguishable: damaging speech planning kills repetition and naming, the two tasks sharing it, while cutting the sound-to-planning pathway kills repetition only with both its regions intact. Three regions is the smallest network in which that contrast can be shown. The caution states plainly that real networks have more regions, bidirectional pathways serving several pairings and enough redundancy that a single cut rarely produces so clean a failure; what the model is for is the inference, not the anatomy.
readmeTopic: how a deficit can come from a cut connection rather than from damage to any region
